parentIntro: The big idea this week: in a number like 342, every digit has a job — the 3 means hundreds, the 4 means tens, the 2 means ones. We want her to see a three-digit number and instantly know what each digit is worth.
watchFor: Zero as a place-holder is the classic trip-up: 407 often gets read or written as 47. If it happens, build both numbers out of blocks side by side and ask “are these the same?” — don’t correct, let her see it.

demo.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
demo.say: Today we are looking at bigger numbers. Watch how umma builds the number three hundred and forty two.

steps.caption: 3 hundreds
steps.say: Here are three big blocks of one hundred. That makes three hundred.

steps.caption: 3 hundreds, 4 tens
steps.say: Now four sticks of ten. That adds forty more.

steps.caption: 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 2 ones
steps.say: And two little ones. Three hundred, forty, two. Three hundred and forty two!

steps.caption: H · T · O = 342
steps.say: We write it with three digits. The 3 means hundreds, the 4 means tens, the 2 means ones.

weDo.model: Use anything around you as blocks — dry pasta, LEGO, or draw squares, sticks and dots on the whiteboard: big square = 100, stick = 10, dot = 1.
steps: Ask Harriet: “How many hundreds do we need?” (2 — draw two big squares.)
Count it back together out loud: “one hundred, two hundred… two hundred and fifty… fifty-one, fifty-two, fifty-three!”
Ask her to write the digits: 2, 5, 3. Point at each and ask what it stands for.

weDo.problem: What number is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones?
weDo.model: Draw it first: four big squares, no sticks, seven dots. The tricky bit is the empty tens place — let her notice there are no sticks.
steps: Let Harriet draw the blocks herself while you read the question again slowly.
Ask: “What do we write when there are NO tens?” (A zero — it holds the place.)
If she writes 47, don’t correct — build 47 in blocks next to it and ask “are these the same?”
Land on 407 together and say it out loud: “four hundred and seven.”

items.text: Harriet has 3 boxes of 100 stickers and 5 loose stickers. How many stickers altogether?
items.say: Harriet has three boxes of one hundred stickers, and five loose stickers. How many stickers altogether?

items.text: The library has 2 shelves of 100 books and 4 stacks of 10 books. How many books?
items.say: The library has two shelves of one hundred books, and four stacks of ten books. How many books is that?

items.text: A jar holds 100 marbles. Umma fills 6 jars and has 2 marbles left over. How many marbles?
items.say: A jar holds one hundred marbles. Umma fills six jars, and has two marbles left over. How many marbles are there?

items.text: Harriet counts 4 bags of 10 shells and 3 loose shells at the beach. How many shells?
items.say: Harriet counts four bags of ten shells, and three loose shells at the beach. How many shells altogether?

items.text: The school bakes 5 trays of 100 cookies and 7 extra cookies. How many cookies?
items.say: The school bakes five trays of one hundred cookies, and seven extra cookies. How many cookies altogether?
What number is one hundred more, than two hundred and fifty?
What number is ten less, than six hundred and forty?
What number comes right after three hundred and ninety nine?

warmupWins.say: What number is one more than ninety nine?
